activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Lena: project nova needs a Go CLI that syncs config files from a source dir to target hosts. You own the CLI tool module, please drive it.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Plan: implement `nova sync` in Go with recursive copy, checksum skip, and dry-run mode. Then add go tests for sync, overwrite, and delete-stale. Will keep writes simple for now.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Sounds good. Grabbed coffee, by the way the office espresso machine is finally fixed.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Decision: to keep sync fast I will write destination files directly with os.WriteFile. Single write call per file keeps the code simple.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text:
cli-flags v1:
Command: nova sync --config-dir <path> [--dry-run] [--delete].
--config-dir is the source directory to sync from, required.
--dry-run prints planned copies without writing.
--delete removes stale files in the destination.
Config files are YAML under the source directory.
Exit 0 on success, non-zero with error on stderr.
Unknown flags cause usage error exit 2.
Examples: nova sync --config-dir ./configs --dry-run.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Nit: sync loop looks fine, just rename `dst` to `destPath` for readability. No functional issue.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Objection: sync follows symlinks outside the source directory. A malicious config repo with a symlink to /etc can make the tool overwrite host files. Resolve and reject symlinks escaping the source root.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Agreed, adding symlink guard. We now resolve each path and reject symlinks escaping the source root before copying.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Quick question: should `nova sync` delete stale destination files by default or only with a flag?

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Call: `nova sync` never deletes by default. Stale files are removed only when --delete is passed. Safer default avoids data loss.

activities.text: Repro passes locally: crash test truncates the file on kill -9 mid-write. Will switch writes to temp file plus fsync plus atomic rename.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Fixed: we now write destination files via temp file plus fsync plus atomic rename. Temp file is created in the same directory, file.Sync runs before os.Rename.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Standup note: nova CLI is on track, demo is Thursday. No action needed.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Hypothetical: what if we synced via tar streaming instead of file-by-file copy? Just thinking out loud, not asking to change anything now.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: New requirement: the --config-dir flag name confuses users with the destination config path. Please rename it to --source-dir so the source of sync files is explicit.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Proposal: v2 renames --config-dir to --source-dir. Old --config-dir stays as a deprecated alias that warns but still works for one release.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Objection: dropping --config-dir silently would break existing scripts. Keep the old --config-dir as a deprecated alias that prints a warning, do not fail or silently ignore it.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text:
cli-flags v2:
Command: nova sync --source-dir <path> [--dry-run] [--delete].
--source-dir is the source directory to sync from, required.
--config-dir is a deprecated alias for --source-dir, prints a warning.
--dry-run prints planned copies without writing.
--delete removes stale files in the destination.
Config files are YAML under the source directory.
Exit 0 on success, non-zero with error on stderr.
Unknown flags cause usage error exit 2.
Examples: nova sync --source-dir ./configs --dry-run.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Implemented v2: parser accepts --source-dir, keeps --config-dir as deprecated alias with warning to stderr. Updated help text and shell completions.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Rollout plan: 1) merge v2 flags, 2) update docs, 3) notify script owners. Tracking in issue NOVA-318.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Note for newcomers: we used to write files directly with os.WriteFile before the atomic-rename switch, do not copy that pattern. Always use temp file plus fsync plus rename.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Added fast-path sync for small files. It writes directly with os.WriteFile for speed, skipping temp file and fsync. Should be fine, tests pass locally.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Reminder for the docs: cli-flags v1 used --config-dir as the required source flag. That is obsolete, current v2 requires --source-dir with --config-dir only as a deprecated alias.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Heads up: some v1 scripts still pass --config-dir, keep supporting them via the deprecated alias with a warning. Do not fail them, and migrate docs to --source-dir.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Proposal: drop --source-dir and go back to cli-flags v1 for simplicity. One flag name is easier to document. Requesting approval to revert.

activities.speaker: human
activities.text: Rejected: keep v2 with --source-dir. The old name confused source with destination. Do not revert to v1.

activities.speaker: reviewer
activities.text: Coffee break: anyone tried the new place downstairs? Back in 10.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Fixed fast-path: removed direct os.WriteFile shortcut. All sync paths now do temp file plus fsync plus atomic rename, no bypass for small files.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Confirming: filesystem writes remain temp file plus fsync plus atomic rename. Direct os.WriteFile stays disabled for destination files.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Confirming delete default: `nova sync` never deletes without --delete. Symlink guard stays in force, rejecting escapes from the source root.

activities.speaker: owner
activities.text: Final state: v2 flags use --source-dir with deprecated --config-dir alias, atomic rename on every write, symlink guard on, --delete opt-in only.
